title_en: Zhao Baohua v. Shanghai Yeningge Hotel Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Jingsheng Industrial Co., Ltd. — dispute over the right to life, health, and bodily integrity
ruling_gist_en: As a hotel operator providing accommodation services, it should perform a duty of safety protection within reasonable limits towards consumers who stay in the hotel. If a hotel operator causes personal injury to a consumer due to safety hazards such as management or service deficiencies, it shall bear civil compensation liability. The lessor of the hotel business premises who fails to properly manage the premises where the incident occurred shall also bear corresponding liability. If the victim is also at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the civil liability of the infringer shall be mitigated in accordance with the principle of comparative negligence.

full_text_en:
Zhao Baohua v. Shanghai Yenige Hotel Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Jingsheng Industrial Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Right to Life, Right to Health, and Right to Physical Integrity

[Ruling Summary]

Hotel operators providing accommodation services shall fulfill a duty of reasonable safety protection towards consumers staying in the hotel. Where hotel operators cause personal injury to consumers due to safety hazards such as management or service deficiencies, they shall bear civil liability for compensation. Where the lessor of the hotel premises fails to properly manage the place where the incident occurred, it shall also bear corresponding liability. Where the victim is also at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the civil liability of the tortfeasor shall be reduced in accordance with the principle of comparative negligence.

Plaintiff: Zhao Baohua, male, 38 years old, Han ethnicity, residing at Huamu Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Defendant: Shanghai Yenige Hotel Co., Ltd., domiciled at Gonghexin Road, Zhabei District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Yang Xu, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Shanghai Jingsheng Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at Gonghexin Road, Zhabei District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Zhou Jingyan, Chairwoman of the company.

The plaintiff, Zhao Baohua, filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Zhabei District People's Court against the defendants, Shanghai Yenige Hotel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Yenige Hotel") and Shanghai Jingsheng Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Jingsheng Company"), concerning a dispute over the right to life, right to health, and right to physical integrity.

Plaintiff's Allegations:

The plaintiff alleged that on the evening of December 14, 2009, he stayed at the defendant Yenige Hotel. At approximately 11:00 p.m. that evening, he went out to buy cigarettes. Following the signs in the hotel corridor, he descended to a safety passage on the first floor. Finding the door locked and unable to exit, he intended to use the elevator in the passage to return upstairs. Unexpectedly, the elevator shaft was vacant (the elevator car had been removed), and there were no warning signs or protective devices outside, causing the plaintiff to step into the empty elevator shaft and fall to the bottom, resulting in injuries. The injuries were assessed as constituting two Grade 10 disabilities. After the incident, Yenige Hotel only paid RMB (hereinafter all amounts in RMB) 40,000 in medical expenses. The building in which the hotel is located is owned by the defendant Jingsheng Company and was leased to Yenige Hotel. According to the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury, Yenige Hotel failed to fulfill its duty of safety protection towards its guests and should bear liability for compensation. Jingsheng Company, as the lessor of defective premises that threatened personal safety, should bear joint and several liability. Therefore, the plaintiff requested that the two defendants jointly compensate him for: medical expenses of RMB 67,119.30; hospital meal subsidy of RMB 274.50; cost of a second-stage treatment of RMB 30,000; nutrition expenses of RMB 4,800; nursing expenses of RMB 4,800; transportation expenses of RMB 1,631; lost wages of RMB 21,394.50; disability compensation of RMB 86,514; expenses for assistive devices of RMB 505; litigation agency fees of RMB 6,000; moral damages of RMB 20,000; document search fees of RMB 80; and appraisal fees of RMB 1,900.

In support of his claim, the plaintiff Zhao Baohua submitted the following evidentiary materials:
First set of evidence: a hotel accommodation invoice, a police report receipt, police station interrogation records, and photographs of the accident scene, to prove that the plaintiff Zhao Baohua checked into the defendant Yenige Hotel on the day of the incident and fell into an empty elevator shaft in the hotel in the early hours of the following day. Second set of evidence: medical history records, medical condition certificates, discharge records, medical expense receipts, daily necessities invoices, nursing fee invoices, transportation fee invoices, assistive device fee invoices, lawyer fee invoices, document search fee invoices, and the plaintiff's individual business license, to prove the plaintiff's medical treatment after the incident and the economic losses caused by the accident. Third set of evidence: a lease contract, to prove the existence of a lease relationship between the two defendants.

Defendant's Defense (Yenige Hotel):

The defendant Yenige Hotel argued that the place where the plaintiff Zhao Baohua fell was not within the leased area of the hotel. The lease contract between Yenige Hotel and the defendant Jingsheng Company explicitly stipulated that the safety passage where the incident occurred was to be used by Jingsheng Company. The plaintiff had actually left the business premises of the hotel that evening, so there was no tortious omission by the hotel in breaching its duty of safety protection. Moreover, after the accident, Yenige Hotel had already paid the plaintiff RMB 40,000 ex gratia. Furthermore, the plaintiff had consumed excessive alcohol at the time of the incident, severely impairing his judgment, and he was himself responsible for the resulting damage. Therefore, Yenige Hotel opposed the plaintiff's claims.

The defendant Yenige Hotel submitted the following evidentiary materials:
Photographs of the accident scene, to prove that a sliding door leading to the incident location had a warning notice stating: "Fire exit. Do not open this door without authorization except in emergency."

Defendant's Defense (Jingsheng Company):

The defendant Jingsheng Company argued that the passageway and the elevator in question were not originally part of the leased premises. The defendant Yenige Hotel requested the removal of the elevator car from the shaft to convert the shaft above the second floor into a storage room for its use. Jingsheng Company agreed, and Yenige Hotel had workers dismantle the elevator car. During the construction, no appropriate safety measures were taken, and the plaintiff Zhao Baohua fell into the empty shaft and was injured. Jingsheng Company claimed it was not at fault for the accident, and the leased premises had no defects. Therefore, Jingsheng Company opposed the plaintiff's claims.

The defendant Jingsheng Company provided the following evidentiary materials:
A supplemental agreement signed by the two defendants, to prove that they had agreed that Yenige Hotel would not damage the building structure during renovation.

During the trial, the plaintiff and the defendants each cross-examined the evidence submitted by the other parties and by the court. The plaintiff Zhao Baohua disputed the authenticity of the photographs submitted by the defendant Yenige Hotel, claiming that the warning signs were posted after the incident. He disputed the relevance of the supplemental agreement provided by the defendant Jingsheng Company, arguing that the agreement between the two defendants could not be invoked against a third party. He had no objection to the expert opinion submitted by the court. The defendant Yenige Hotel disputed the invoices for daily necessities, nursing fees, lawyer fees, and document search fees submitted by the plaintiff, arguing they were irrelevant to the case. It had no objection to the other evidence submitted by the plaintiff, the supplemental agreement submitted by the defendant Jingsheng Company, and the expert opinion submitted by the court. Jingsheng Company disputed the statement made by Yenige Hotel employee Hu Chunhua in the police station interrogation record that the elevator shaft was not within the leased area of Yenige Hotel, arguing it was factually incorrect. Its opinions on the other evidence submitted by the plaintiff were consistent with Yenige Hotel's. It had no objection to the photographs submitted by Yenige Hotel or the expert opinion submitted by the court.

The court heard the parties' cross-examination opinions and admitted the following evidence to which neither the plaintiff nor the defendants objected: the hotel accommodation invoice, the police report receipt, medical history records, medical condition certificates, discharge records, medical expense receipts, transportation fee invoices, assistive device fee invoices, the expert opinion, the plaintiff Zhao Baohua's individual business license, and the lease contract. Regarding the contested evidence, the court reviewed and certified as follows: 1. The photographs of the accident scene submitted by the plaintiff and the police station interrogation records of Zhu Changsheng and Hu Chunhua formed a chain of evidence proving the fact that the plaintiff fell from a height into the empty elevator shaft and the scene of the incident; they were persuasive and were admitted. 2. The invoices for daily necessities, nursing fees, lawyer fees, and document search fees submitted by the plaintiff met the formal requirements of tax invoices; the court confirmed their authenticity, but the specific items and amounts of compensation actually recoverable would be explained item by item later in accordance with specific regulations. 3. The photographs submitted by the defendant Yenige Hotel were not corroborated by other relevant evidence regarding the time they were taken; therefore, the authenticity and relevance of this evidence were not admitted. 4. The supplemental agreement provided by the defendant Jingsheng Company, although authentic and valid, only stipulated the rights and obligations of the two parties regarding the leased premises and did not involve the passageway or the elevator shaft on the first floor; therefore, the court did not admit the relevance of this evidence.

Facts Found by the Court (First Instance, Shanghai Zhabei District People's Court):

On the evening of December 14, 2009, the plaintiff Zhao Baohua stayed at the defendant Yenige Hotel, located at No. 452 Gonghexin Road, Shanghai. At approximately 11:00 p.m. that evening, Zhao Baohua passed through the hotel's No. 4 passage and entered a ground-floor passage near Zhongxing Road within the building. Because the elevator shaft in this passage was vacant (the elevator car had been removed) and had no protective devices, the plaintiff, who had been drinking alcohol, stepped into the empty elevator shaft and fell to the bottom, sustaining injuries. After the incident, Zhao Baohua called 110 at approximately 4:00 a.m. the following day. Police arrived at the scene and took him to the Second Affiliated Hospital of the Second Military Medical University for treatment. He was diagnosed with a right subtrochanteric fracture, a left distal clavicular fracture, fractures of the left 8th and 9th ribs, and a left coracoid process fracture. He was hospitalized that day, underwent open reduction and internal fixation surgery for the right subtrochanteric fracture and left clavicular fracture on December 17, 2009, and was discharged on December 28, 2009. He subsequently made multiple outpatient follow-up visits. During this period, the plaintiff paid medical expenses of RMB 66,394.33 and assistive device expenses of RMB 528.

The court further found that the defendant Yenige Hotel and the defendant Jingsheng Company had signed a house lease contract in which Jingsheng Company leased the premises at No. 452 Gonghexin Road to Yenige Hotel. The contract noted that the ground-floor passage near Zhongxing Road (i.e., the accident passage) was to be used by Jingsheng Company. After signing the lease contract, Yenige Hotel, with Jingsheng Company's consent, removed the elevator car from the shaft in the passage and converted the elevator shaft above the second floor into a storage room for Yenige Hotel's use. During the construction, no protective devices were installed for the empty elevator shaft.

The court also found that the plaintiff Zhao Baohua was an individual business operator engaged in the retail of clothing at Shop B2-24, North Plaza, No. 2002 Century Avenue, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

During the proceedings, upon the application of the plaintiff Zhao Baohua, the court commissioned the Forensic Identification Center of the Institute of Forensic Science, Ministry of Justice, to conduct a forensic medical evaluation of Zhao Baohua's disability grade and the periods for rest, nursing, and nutrition following his injuries. The center issued an expert opinion stating: The examined person, Zhao Baohua, fell from the empty elevator shaft to the bottom, sustaining a right subtrochanteric fracture, a left distal clavicular fracture, a left coracoid process fracture, left rib fractures, and left pleural effusion. The sequelae of limited function of the left upper limb and right lower limb resulting from the above injuries correspond to Grade 10 and Grade 10 disabilities, respectively, in road traffic accidents. The rest period for the first stage of treatment following the injury is 180 days, the nursing period is 120 days, and the nutrition period is 120 days. If a second stage of treatment is performed in the future, the rest period will be 30 days, the nursing period will be 15 days, and the nutrition period will be 15 days.

During the trial, both the plaintiff Zhao Baohua and the defendant Yenige Hotel confirmed that Yenige Hotel had paid Zhao Baohua RMB 40,000 in medical expenses after the incident and agreed to deduct this amount from Yenige Hotel's final compensation determined in this case. Zhao Baohua also admitted to having consumed alcohol before the incident.

Opinion of the Court (First Instance, Shanghai Zhabei District People's Court):

The court of first instance held that the parties had the following disputes regarding facts and the application of law: First, whether the defendant Yenige Hotel had fulfilled a reasonable duty of safety protection; second, whether the defendant Jingsheng Company, as the lessor, should bear supervisory responsibility given that the lessee Yenige Hotel removed the elevator car during renovation; and third, whether the plaintiff Zhao Baohua himself was at fault for the occurrence of the accident.

Regarding the first disputed issue, the court held that where a natural person, legal person, or other organization engaged in business operations such as accommodation, catering, entertainment, or other social activities fails to fulfill its duty of safety protection within reasonable limits, thereby causing personal injury to another person, the right holder to compensation may request that it bear corresponding compensation liability, and the people's court shall support such a request. The defendant Yenige Hotel, as a business providing accommodation services, should ensure the personal safety of consumers staying in the hotel within reasonable limits and avoid personal injury caused by management or service deficiencies. Based on the evidence in this case, the defendant Yenige Hotel failed to provide obvious warnings of potential injuries or accidents. It argued that it had posted a warning sign on the sliding door leading to the accident passage. However, according to the statements of both parties, there was no lighting at the location of the sliding door that evening. Even if such a sign existed, it was wholly insufficient to serve as a warning. Regarding Yenige Hotel's argument that the accident passage and the elevator were not within the leased area and therefore it was not liable, the court held that the accident passage was a relatively enclosed area accessible via a safety exit within Yenige Hotel. At the time of the incident, the elevator shaft in this area was vacant because the car had been removed. Yenige Hotel was aware of this situation and had de facto control over the accident passage and the elevator, yet it failed to take adequate safety precautions. The safety hazard in its service provision had a direct causal relationship with the damage suffered by the plaintiff Zhao Baohua. Therefore, Yenige Hotel should bear civil liability for compensation for the accident. The court did not accept Yenige Hotel's relevant arguments.

Regarding the second disputed issue, the court held that the defendant Jingsheng Company and the defendant Yenige Hotel had signed a house lease contract. Subsequently, Jingsheng Company agreed to Yenige Hotel's removal of the elevator car from the ground-floor passage near Zhongxing Road and the modification of the elevator shaft above the second floor for Yenige Hotel's use. This could be considered an amendment to the content of the lease contract. However, the amendment did not involve the accident passage or the first-floor elevator shaft. Therefore, Jingsheng Company, as the right holder, remained obligated to manage the premises. During the proceedings, Yenige Hotel indicated its willingness to assume the corresponding liability of Jingsheng Company, and the plaintiff Zhao Baohua agreed. The unanimous agreement of the parties was not contrary to law, and the court granted its approval.

Regarding the third disputed issue, the court held that where the victim is also at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the tortfeasor's civil liability may be reduced. The plaintiff Zhao Baohua, as a person with full civil capacity, should have exercised reasonable care for his own actions to ensure his own safety. The "Shanghai Public Security Bureau Case Receipt Form" dated December 15, 2009, recorded: "Upon arrival, the police understood that an empty elevator shaft on the first floor, near the Zhongxing Road corner opposite the fire door of the hotel's No. 4 passage, lacked protective measures, causing an intoxicated guest to fall into the elevator shaft." In light of the plaintiff's own statements, it could be determined that Zhao Baohua, after consuming alcohol and without lighting, entered the accident passage, failed to observe his surroundings carefully, and stepped into the empty elevator shaft. He failed to exercise ordinary care, and his consumption of alcohol, which affected his normal judgment, was also related to the occurrence of the accident. Therefore, in accordance with the principle of comparative negligence, the liability of the defendant Yenige Hotel could be appropriately reduced.

The court found the plaintiff Zhao Baohua's claims for medical expenses, hospital meal subsidy, nutrition expenses, nursing expenses, transportation expenses, lost wages, disability compensation, assistive device expenses, moral damages, litigation agency fees, and document search fees to be legally grounded and supported. The specific compensation amounts and calculation methods were as follows: 1. Medical expenses, assistive device expenses, and document search fees: Based on the invoices provided by the plaintiff, the court determined the actual amounts to be RMB 66,394.33, RMB 528, and RMB 80, respectively. 2. Hospital meal subsidy: Calculated at RMB 20 per day for 14 days, less RMB 5.50 for self-paid food during hospitalization, resulting in RMB 274.50. 3. Nutrition and nursing expenses: Referencing relevant regulations and the expert opinion from the appraisal authority, the court determined nutrition and nursing expenses to be RMB 4,800 each. 4. Transportation expenses: The plaintiff and defendants agreed on the base amount of RMB 1,631, which the court accepted. 5. Lost wages: Based on the plaintiff's occupation in retail clothing, the average municipal employee wage for the preceding year, and the rest period determined in the expert opinion, the court calculated his lost wages as RMB 21,394.50. 6. Disability compensation: Determined by the court based on the disability grade determined by the appraisal authority, the annual per capita disposable income of the resident area of the court for the preceding year multiplied by 20 years, and referencing the calculation standards for multiple disabilities. 7. Moral damages: The accident caused the plaintiff to suffer personal injury and disability, bringing him mental pain. Therefore, the court determined an appropriate amount at its discretion in accordance with relevant regulations. 8. Litigation agency fees: The lawyer fees the plaintiff paid for employing a lawyer for the litigation were also his loss and should be compensated. The specific amount would be determined at the court's discretion according to relevant regulations and the actual circumstances of this case. Regarding the plaintiff's claim for future medical expenses for a second-stage treatment, since these expenses had not yet been incurred, they were not addressed in this case. The plaintiff could make a separate claim in the future based on actual circumstances. The defendant Yenige Hotel should bear corresponding civil liability for the above-mentioned medical expenses, hospital meal subsidy, nutrition expenses, nursing expenses, transportation expenses, lost wages, disability compensation, assistive device expenses, and document search fees based on its degree of fault. Furthermore, to avoid repeated litigation, the RMB 40,000 already paid by Yenige Hotel would be deducted from the compensation amount determined in this case.

Accordingly, in accordance with Articles 119 and 131 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury, the Shanghai Zhabei District People's Court rendered the following judgment on February 11, 2011:

The defendant, Shanghai Yenige Hotel Co., Ltd., shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, make a one-time compensation payment to the plaintiff Zhao Baohua of RMB 157,000 (of which RMB 40,000 has already been paid) for medical expenses, hospital meal subsidy, nutrition expenses, nursing expenses, transportation expenses, lost wages, disability compensation, assistive device expenses, moral damages, litigation agency fees, and document search fees.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, neither party filed an appeal, and the judgment became legally effective.
